message.content: In lions, one of the most striking examples of a dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. The mane is largely governed by a dominant allele that influences the growth of dense, dark hair around the head and neck. While females lack this trait, the dominant allele ensures that when it is present in a male, the mane will develop, giving him the iconic appearance that is often associated with the species.
